solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pole draws attention to short Welshman

parts.note: to flag something is to draw attention to it, so 'flags'

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: Taffy is a traditional, now dated nickname for a Welshman

explanation.surface: A tall pole catches the eye beside a Welshman of small stature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last letter from TAFFY, leaving TAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the upright pole from which a flag is flown, so it is a kind of pole.

clue.text: Room to manoeuvre in sheltered passage

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a way is a path or passage

explanation.surface: Someone finds space to move about in a protected corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom of action or margin for movement, an idiomatic synonym for room to manoeuvre.

clue.text: Pre-tax report on royal purveyor

indicators.note: report signals that the word is heard rather than read, so its sound is used

parts.note: gross pay or income is the amount before tax is taken off
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: An account of earnings before tax is made about a supplier to the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The word GROSS spoken sounds like the first syllable of the answer, written GROC.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer sells and supplies food and household goods, so is a purveyor of provisions.

clue.text: Company tore up arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters means they are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm has ripped up a deal it had made.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of touring performers, such as actors or dancers.

clue.text: Cricketer's slender limb

parts.note: fine can mean thin or slender
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A cricket player has a thin leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fine leg is a fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side, and also the fielder standing there; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine leg names the fielder in that position, so the cricketer stationed behind the batsman on the leg side.

clue.text: Vivid constant scowl adopted by foul drunk

parts.note: c is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by the following piece, so one sits inside the other
drunk suggests the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: to lour is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: A drunkard of foul temper keeps up a lurid, permanent scowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the four letters of the second clue word into OFUL, and 'adopted by' puts the frown inside it after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourful means bright and full of colour, a synonym for vivid.

clue.text: Unknown coin got in change

indicators.note: change means the letters are altered into another order, playing on loose coins

explanation.surface: A mysterious coin turned up among some loose change.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incognito has a concealed identity, so is unknown to those around them.

clue.text: After ten years, North Carolina finds energy to reveal corruption

indicators.note: after says the state abbreviation follows the ten-year period

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years
NC is the US postal abbreviation for North Carolina
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Ten years on, a US state discovers the power to expose sleaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral decline and self-indulgence, a synonym for corruption.

clue.text: There's oxygen in breathing apparatus prior to end of dive, so relax

indicators.note: prior to says what comes before the final letter that follows
in places the oxygen symbol inside the organ of breathing

parts.note: a lung is the body's own apparatus for breathing
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of dive

explanation.surface: A diver checks the air in the tank before finishing the dive, so can take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to recline or loaf idly, a synonym for relax.

clue.text: See 18
Got crushed by snake in South American city

indicators.note: crushed by means held tight inside the snake that constricts

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: Someone was squeezed by a serpent in a Latin American town.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia in South America.

clue.text: A long tow rope is uncoiled for 20 sport

indicators.note: uncoiled suggests a rope unravelled, so the letters are loosened and rearranged

parts.note: L is an abbreviation of long, as in longitude

explanation.surface: A lengthy towing line is let out for use in a watery game.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points to the answer at 20 across, AQUATIC, giving 'aquatic sport'.
explanation.definitionFit: Water polo is a team ball game played in a swimming pool, an aquatic sport.

clue.text: Bowled French XI in inspired frenzy — a momentous time

parts.note: b is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: in puts the French number inside the fury

parts.note: rage is a frenzy, here one that is inspired, as in all the rage
onze is French for eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A French football eleven were knocked over in a fevered frenzy at a historic moment.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is the Roman numeral eleven; in French that is ONZE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronze Age was a major prehistoric era when bronze tools replaced stone, a momentous period in history.

clue.text: Alvin Stardust, for instance, is somewhat hammy — no, due spectacular comeback

indicators.note: comeback means the run of letters is read backwards
somewhat means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A glam-rock singer, rather over the top, makes a dazzling return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes MYNODUESP from inside 'hammy — no, due spectacular', and 'comeback' turns it around. Alvin Stardust was a 1970s British pop singer whose real name was Bernard Jewry.
explanation.definitionFit: Alvin Stardust was a stage name, an example of a false name adopted by a performer.

clue.text: Bats maul pairs of koalas typically

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: describing what typically belongs to koalas, pouched mammals

indicators.note: bats in the sense of crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Flying bats savage couples of Australian bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the animals but is the anagram signal, meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Koalas carry their young in a pouch, so as an adjective marsupial describes them typically.

clue.text: Bad Mailer novel is exceptional

indicators.note: novel as new or fresh means the letters take a new arrangement, playing on Norman Mailer the novelist

explanation.surface: A poor book by Norman Mailer is still remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Mailer was an American novelist, so 'novel' poses as a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirable means deserving praise, close in sense to exceptional or excellent.

clue.text: See 13
See 24
Perfume's elegance and odour somehow not right

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come out in some new order

explanation.surface: A scent's refinement and smell are not quite correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes one R from the pooled letters before 'somehow' rearranges them; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light scented water, a kind of perfume.

clue.text: Crisp and expanding girdle fabric

indicators.note: the words girdle, or encircle, the letters sitting within them

explanation.surface: A crisp, stretchy corset fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandex is a stretchy synthetic elastic fibre used in sportswear, so a fabric.

clue.text: A qualified university algologist tended only the tips attached to one cold water plant

indicators.note: only the tips means just the first letter of each of these words is used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A trained university botanist looked after only the tops of a chilly pond plant.
explanation.walkthrough: An algologist studies algae, making the botany picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an aquatic is a plant that grows in or near water.

clue.text: Teams up regularly with Hull bird

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Teams join forces now and then with a bird from a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the city, but it is Rod Hull, a British TV entertainer famous for his unruly puppet, Emu.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Hull's puppet act was a large flightless Australian bird, so his bird.

clue.text: Hooked up with eccentric admirer

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: Someone got together with a quirky fan.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hooked up, informally, is to be paired off or wed, so married.

clue.text: Perversely Sid and Una like Harpo's lines

indicators.note: perversely means contrarily, so the letters are put in a contrary order

explanation.surface: Two awkward people are compared with a silent comedian's script.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpo Marx, of the Marx Brothers, never spoke on screen, so his lines were never said.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that are never spoken are unspoken, like the mute performer's.

clue.text: Domineering woman in fight over job dismissal

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a battle is a fight
the axe is informal for being sacked from a job

explanation.surface: A bossy woman is caught up in a dispute about someone being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle-axe is an idiom for an aggressive, overbearing older woman.

clue.text: Emphasise pronunciation

definitions.meaning: to stress a syllable or point
a regional or national way of speaking

explanation.definitionFit: To accent is to stress; an accent is also a distinctive manner of pronunciation.

clue.text: End-of-term activity is hard work

definitions.meaning: giving birth at the end of a pregnancy's full term

explanation.surface: Studies wrapping up at the end of school term are a real slog.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is childbirth at the end of pregnancy, and also strenuous work.

clue.text: Get actor a bespoke item from wardrobe

indicators.note: bespoke means made to order, so the letters are remade into a new order

explanation.surface: Fetch a performer a tailored costume piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat, an item kept in a wardrobe of clothes.

clue.text: Harpo mangled new line at end of paragraph

indicators.note: mangled means badly mutilated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Harpo Marx garbled a fresh line at the end of his piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In typesetting, a lone opening or closing line of a paragraph stranded on another page or column is called an orphan.

clue.text: Seedy motel — site that's an excuse for a kiss and a cuddle

definitions.text: that's an excuse for a kiss and a cuddle

indicators.note: seedy means run down and disreputable, so the letters fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A sleazy roadside motel is a place for romantic encounters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the custom of kissing under hanging sprigs at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: By tradition people kiss under a sprig of this plant at Christmas, so it excuses a kiss.

clue.text: Say why member of nobility has Dandy's latest annual

indicators.note: say signals the word spoken, which sounds like a letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y
an earl is a member of the British peerage

indicators.note: latest picks the final letter of the comic's name

explanation.surface: Ask why a nobleman owns the newest edition of a comic annual.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy was a long-running British children's comic with a yearly annual.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearly and annual are synonyms, both meaning once each year.

clue.text: Risk Dixieland intro in rave tune remix

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the rearranged music
remix means the letters are mixed into a new order, suiting the music theme
intro picks the first letter of Dixieland

explanation.surface: A jazz opening dropped into a rave tune remix is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remix' rearranges RAVE TUNE, and 'in' puts D inside to make ADVENTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a risky undertaking, and the verb means to risk or dare.
